newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start higher on Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start higher on Dow rebound.

text.p: The CAC index opened about half a percent higher, bouncing after Wall Street's overnight partial recovery from two days of heavy losses, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 17.07 points or 0.66 percent at 2,598.89 at 0807 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 21 at 2,598 from Tuesday's close.
The market was also underpinned by the bond market, but brokers did not exclude a further downward correction in coming weeks.
Volume was 600 million francs, including 450 million in blue-chip shares.

Key data due today are the U.S. February factory orders, due at 1500 GMT. Finance Minister Jean Arthuis is expected to confirm this afternoon the government's 1997 growth forecast of 2.3 percent in GDP.

Thomson-CSF was up 3.84 percent at 192 francs in wake of newspaper articles saying that Britain's GEC Plc had submitted a bod for the state's 58-percent stake last Friday, rivalling bids by both Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Groupe.
The Finance Minstry had no comment on the reports while at GEC no one was immediately available for comment.
The government is expected to decide on Friday which of the bids it received are valid and can be considered.
Lagardere was up 1.71 percent at 181 francs. The company will annnounce its results after the market closes later on Wednesday.
Lyonnaise des Eaux, which has a board meeting on Wednesday, will publish its 1996 results on Thursday morning.
On Tuesday, the supervisory board of Suez said it was unanimously favourable to a proposed merger with Lyonnaise. The two boards will have special meetings on April 11 to discuss the merger terms.
Lyonnaise was down 0.54 percent at 551 francs and Suez was up 0.56 percent at 287.5 francs.
